task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the projects funded through Greywillow's first youth-budget panel. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 15, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Greywillow Council ratified a $40,000 package recommended by its first youth-budget panel on Sept. 14, 2026.
The package allocates $18,000 for seating at the skate area, $12,000 for shared rehearsal equipment and $10,000 for a community garden's water connection.
The 18-member youth panel recommended the combined package by a vote of 15-3.
Panel members were recruited through schools and youth organizations, not elected in a citywide vote.
The council retained responsibility for authorizing expenditure and checking whether each proposed project could be delivered on city-controlled sites.
The panel considered 11 eligible proposals after staff screened out submissions outside the program's budget or location rules.
The panel's youth chair said in the supplied statement, "We had to decide what could be shared, not just what each of us wanted for our own group."
The skate-area seating will include spaces for people watching rather than taking part, but the grant does not rebuild the skating surface.
Rehearsal equipment will be stored and booked through the youth center, not transferred permanently to a single band.
The garden water connection requires a final utility estimate before work can be ordered.
If that estimate exceeds the allocation, the garden proposal must return for a funding decision rather than automatically draw from the other two awards.
Youth-services director Amra Vale said, "The panel made real choices, and the city still has to carry out the unglamorous work of buying and installing things."
Some panel members wanted a transport project, but a transport submission was screened out because its requested funding exceeded the entire available budget.
Staff will publish reasons for eligibility decisions so rejected applicants can distinguish a rule-based exclusion from the panel's preferences.
The city has not announced installation dates for all three projects or claimed that any is already operating.
The grant is capital funding and does not pay for a permanent new youth-worker position.
The youth center has agreed to manage bookings and routine checks of the rehearsal equipment within its existing program.
Panel members will be invited to review procurement updates and inspect completed projects with city staff.
The city paid panel members' travel costs but did not require them to donate money to any selected project.
Meetings rotated between the youth center and a library meeting room to avoid making one school the permanent host.
The council will decide whether to repeat the program after reviewing delivery and who took part in the first panel.
No citywide measure of young residents' preferences or long-term participation outcome accompanies the funding decision.

forbidden_additions: A citywide youth election or preference mandate.
Completed projects, guaranteed delivery dates or automatic transfers between awards.
Permanent staff funding or equipment ownership by one band.
preserve: Youth choice within defined public spending and delivery responsibilities.
The three allocations, shared-use conditions and unresolved utility estimate.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
